voices.name: Multilingual
voices.persona: Chatterbox as it comes, with no one cloned into it. Neutral, reliable, and the fastest thing here to start with.

voices.name: Phil
voices.persona: Enjoys the material and lets you hear it. Good for adventure, comedy, and anything with dialogue worth acting.

voices.name: David
voices.persona: Articulate and slightly formal. Suits history, biography and anything with footnotes.

voices.name: Ruth
voices.persona: Unshowy and exact, the way a good documentary is narrated. Never gets between you and the sentence.

voices.name: Elizabeth
voices.persona: Reads as though the book matters and you have all evening. Best for long novels you intend to finish.

voices.name: Bob
voices.persona: Low, slow and settled. The one to fall asleep to, which is either the point or the problem.

voices.name: Adrian
voices.persona: Has opinions about the characters and does the voices. Excellent for classics, distracting for a manual.

voices.name: Cori
voices.persona: Precise and a little dry. Handles complicated prose without letting it become a performance.

voices.name: Karen
voices.persona: The voice of someone reading to a room. Unhurried, fond of the characters, good company at bedtime.

voices.name: Kara
voices.persona: Keeps things moving. Suits non-fiction and anything you want to get through rather than linger over.

voices.name: Mark
voices.persona: Even-tempered to the point of being restful. The safe choice for a book you will listen to for twenty hours.
